summary: The patient presents with a 3-day history of sore throat, worsening with swallowing and localized to the left side, accompanied by fever (101.8 F). Patient reports mild nasal congestion but denies cough, nausea, vomiting, or rash. Notable exposure to strep throat from family member last week.
differential: Streptococcal pharyngitis (high suspicion due to exposure)
Peritonsillar abscess (due to unilateral pain and odynophagia)
key_observations: Fever of 101.8 F reported last night
Recent household contact with strep throat
doctor_action_options: Culture if rapid test is negative
recommended_next_steps: Perform physical examination of pharynx and tonsils for exudates, erythema, or asymmetry
Consider throat culture if rapid test is negative
Assess for signs of peritonsillar abscess if indicated by exam
relevant_prior_history: No prior history available in record for this patient.
missing_or_uncertain_details: Presence of tonsillar exudate or hypertrophy
